NEW Nightglass Courier TWO-PANEL story page for03 and04: a VERTICAL portrait canvas approximately1024×1536, TWO full-width horizontal tiers divided by one narrow plain gutter. No words, signs with writing, balloons, captions or UI. Both beats are SILENT. TOP03 — ordinary broad PUBLIC LANE journey toward the east washhouse, laundry lines/work traffic and distant city terraces. A clear three-quarter SIDE view shows Daro pulling his EMPTY two-wheel cart forward toward screenRIGHT. He is AHEAD of the cart walking normally, with BOTH BARE HANDS each firmly gripping ONE of its TWO wooden handles, raising the handles to a comfortable carrying height. The cart rolls on EXACTLY TWO large spoked wheels on ONE shared axle. BOTH wheel rims remain in visible contact with the SAME level paving. Tilting the handles up raises the TWO rigid parking feet under the front corners COMPLETELY OFF the paving; show unmistakable daylight under BOTH parking-foot tips, not a leg dragging along the road or a floating wheel. Use a perspective that exposes these actual contacts and gaps, not an occluding heroic camera. Keep full cart and his grips in frame, with useful paving below wheels and feet. Gray pad flat inside lowwoodbed, ONE loose brown strap rests across the EMPTY bed; no cargo, passenger or magic. This is the ordinary tilt-and-pull mechanism of the established cart, not a four-wheel wagon or extra axle.

Aren and Sera walk alongside at an ordinary pace, not riding/climbing/cart-carrying. BOTTOM04 — NEW PLACE ESTABLISHMENT, mostly architecture with NO large foreground principal cast. One modest working WASHHOUSE across a small level paved forecourt, seen from a FRONT-RIGHT oblique viewpoint so its exterior wall and the near dry interior can be read together. A broad OPEN MAIN DOORWAY is on pictureRIGHT. A low raised STONE WATER-SILL crosses this doorway to contain ordinary washwater INSIDE; show its useful unbroken supported shape. Just LEFT of this doorway on the SAME wall is an already-CLOSED NARROW mending SERVICE HATCH: one clearly shut rectangular wooden side-hinged shutter above a FIXED broad stone sill at ordinary handover height. The hatch is visibly narrower than a collection basket, yet broad enough for one compact hand-carried bundle later. It is not another full-size door, a balcony, invented tunnel or boarded-up disaster.

INSIDE the main doorway, the camera sees a plain supported DRY WOODEN BENCH with legs and a dry standing-floor strip along the near LEFT wall BEHIND the closed hatch. The bench extends into sight THROUGH THE OPEN MAIN DOOR, not through a transparent shutter. Farther inside/right is a distinct active WET washing lane with supported rinse tubs/table, light steam and a couple of small anonymous workstaff silhouettes. Do not introduce a recognizable Edda or test bundles yet; those have their own later story introductions. Dry bench/floor stay separate from wet work, and all supports sit on actual floor.

OUTSIDE, continuous level public paving forms a SMALL FORECOURT in front of this same wall, with a clear standing/cart frontage below the hatch and ordinary room for people to use the main door. A single low STONE DRINKING TROUGH is plainly visible at the far end of the little forecourt, across the left foreground, physically connected to the hatch by that SAME uninterrupted paving. Establish doorway, CLOSED hatch, dry interior bench, level frontage and trough in ONE coherent view. No abyss, bridge, lift, long district route, customer recipient, exterior storage pile or goods. Warm practical city morning; the place is busy and maintained, not an emergency. Later panels will use this exact ordinary geography, so give the hatch and trough distinctive simple silhouettes rather than hiding them behind plants or foreground people.
